title: Scoped Guards and Underscore
goal: Learn how binding names affect value lifetimes.

sections.text: You use variables in Python or Java to hold values until they go out of scope.

sections.caption: Guards execute cleanup code when dropped.

sections.text: A standard binding like `let _g = Guard;` keeps the value alive until the end of the enclosing block.

sections.caption: let _ drops the temporary right away.

sections.text: The underscore `_` is a pattern that matches anything without binding it. Because no variable holds the value, Rust drops it on that exact line.
This distinction matters when RAII guards hold locks or manage state. Using `let _` releases the guard before your work even starts.

explanation: Learn how binding names affect value lifetimes.
